subject: MarinerAI — Dedicated capacity onboarding: scope & sprint plan
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Lucas Reed <lucas@mariner.ai>
Cc: Sasha Park <sasha.park@mariner.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 10:12:00 -0000
Subject: MarinerAI — Dedicated capacity onboarding: scope & sprint plan

Hi Lucas / Sasha,

Great to meet you on the call yesterday — excited to get MarinerAI onto a dedicated GPU pool. To keep momentum, I wanted to outline the things we'll need to scope and propose a 3-week onboarding sprint. Can you confirm the items below by EOD Thursday?

1) Target models & expected token profile (avg prompt tokens / avg generated tokens).
2) Typical sustained qps and peak concurrency (15 min rolling peak), and any planned batch inference jobs.
3) Preferred regions for data/compute (US-west / US-east / EU etc).
4) Compliance/contract must-haves (data residency, audit log retention).
5) Procurement lead & PO timing (if you need a SOW / PO to start provisioning).

Attached: onboarding_checklist.pdf (one-pager) and capacity_template.csv for perf numbers.

My proposed sprint (high-level):
- Week 0: Kickoff + data exchange + capacity template
- Week 1: Pool provisioning & baseline perf tests (staging)
- Week 2: Autoscale rules, warm-pool validation, DR failover test
- Week 3: Go-live ramp + rollback playbook handed to CS/ops

Two quick notes on autoscale: we generally recommend a small always-on footprint (min_nodes) plus an elastic warm pool to meet brief spikes without cold startups. We'll tailor the scale step and cooldowns based on your latency SLOs.

If that timeline looks good, I'll schedule an internal ops/infra pre-check and send a draft SOW.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: onboarding_checklist.pdf (1.2 KB stub), capacity_template.csv (800 B stub)
From: Lucas Reed <lucas@mariner.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sasha Park <sasha.park@mariner.ai>, procurement@mariner.ai
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 16:04:00 -0000
Subject: Re: MarinerAI — Dedicated capacity onboarding: scope & sprint plan

Hi Neha — thanks for the clear plan. Quick answers below and I've attached our internal traffic profile export.

1) Models: open-llama-70b and a custom fine-tune for summarization. Avg prompt ~120 tokens, avg gen ~480 tokens.
2) Sustained: ~12 qps (text-gen) sustained, typical 95th-concurrency ~45 requests, expected peak (marketing campaign) up to ~220 concurrent sessions for ~20 minutes windows. We also run nightly batch scoring jobs (higher throughput, can be scheduled).
3) Regions: primary us-west1, fallback us-east1. No EU requirement for now.
4) Compliance: standard NDA + SOC2 in progress; need audit log retention of 90 days.
5) Procurement: CC'd procurement@mariner.ai (they will confirm PO timing). Expect PO within 10 business days after SOW.

Happy to do a 30-min ops workshop next week to walk through traffic patterns.

—Lucas
VP of Engineering | MarinerAI
lucas@mariner.ai

Attachments: mariner_traffic_export_20290521.csv (14 KB stub)
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2029 09:08:00 -0000
Subject: RE: MarinerAI — internal alignment: initial sizing + policy proposal

Neha / Jordan — pulling this into ops lane. Notes from Lucas's profile: sustained 12 qps, peaks to 220 for short bursts, nightly batch jobs. My recommendation:

- Pool topology: Dedicated A100 80GB baseline. Start with min_nodes = 3 (handles baseline + warm cache)
- Warm pool: provision warm_burst = 8 nodes available within 60s to cover short 20-min spikes; that gives headroom to ~100 concurrency immediately while autoscaler adds remainder.
- Autoscale policy: scale_step = 4 nodes, cooldown = 90s, target_token_latency <= 250ms p50 for text-gen flows. For batch scoring, route to separate queue with scheduled windows.
- DR/Failover: Primary us-west1; failover to us-east1 with cold-start tolerance for up to 5 minutes. We'll document the rollback playbook.

Need two things to start provisioning: quota approval from infra (A100s in us-west1) and signed SOW. Jordan, can you pick up the infra quota ticket? I'll draft the scaling runbook and perf test checklist.

-Monica
Senior Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.ai
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Lucas Reed <lucas@mariner.ai>, Sasha Park <sasha.park@mariner.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, procurement@mariner.ai
Date: Thu, 23 May 2029 13:32:00 -0000
Subject: Re: MarinerAI — Dedicated capacity onboarding: scope & sprint plan

Thanks Lucas — that profile is exactly the type of info we need. Attached is a first-pass SOW (sow_mariner_draft_v1.pdf) that reflects Monica's proposal (min_nodes=3, warm_burst=8, autoscale step 4, cooldown 90s).

A couple operational clarifications:
- Warm-pool billing: warm nodes are billed at reduced idle price while reserved and are immediately usable; we'll show estimates in the SOW appendix.
- Audit logs: we can retain event-level logs for 90 days as requested; if you need longer retention we can add an archive to your private bucket.

I'll schedule the ops workshop for next Wednesday (May 29) at 14:00 PT unless you suggest otherwise. Procurement, if you can confirm PO windows we can start quota requests immediately.

Regards,
Neha
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.ai
